content.title: Definition, epidemiology and prognosis

sections.heading: Definition of heart failure
sections.text: Heart failure (HF) is described as a clinical syndrome with cardinal symptoms (e.g., breathlessness, ankle swelling, fatigue) and signs (e.g., elevated jugular venous pressure, pulmonary crackles, peripheral oedema) due to structural and/or functional abnormality of the heart resulting in elevated intracardiac pressures and/or inadequate cardiac output at rest and/or during exercise. Identifying the aetiology of underlying cardiac dysfunction is mandatory because specific pathology determines treatment. Most commonly HF is due to myocardial dysfunction (systolic, diastolic, or both); valvular, pericardial, endocardial disease, and rhythm/conduction abnormalities may also contribute.

sections.heading: Terminology
sections.text: HF is classified by left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) into distinct phenotypes. Reduced LVEF is defined as ≤40% and designated HFrEF. LVEF 41–49% is considered mildly reduced (HFmrEF) and may benefit from therapies similar to HFrEF. LVEF ≥50% with symptoms/signs and structural/functional abnormalities or raised natriuretic peptides is HFpEF. The guideline references tables and sections for detailed diagnostic criteria and notes measurement variability of LVEF by echocardiography.

sections.heading: Selected abbreviations shown on the page
sections.text: Includes entries such as SGLT2 = sodium-glucose co-transporter 2; T2DM = type 2 diabetes mellitus; and multiple HF-related abbreviations (HFrEF, HFmrEF, HFpEF, LVEF, NYHA, ICD, LBBB, etc.).

key_points: HF is a syndrome, not a single pathological diagnosis; requires identification of underlying aetiology for management.
Classification by LVEF: HFrEF (≤40%), HFmrEF (41–49%), HFpEF (≥50%).
Measurement of LVEF by echocardiography is variable; classifications guide treatment decisions based on prior trials.
